b076459471.q: How did Saadaa grow from December 2020 launch to profitability and what were the early revenue milestones
b076459471.a: Saadaa started in December 2020 with monthly revenue of 2 lakh rupees, quadrupled revenue in the next month, and tripled the business again after the first quarter of operations. By the fifth month of operations, they were doing about 40 lakhs in monthly business, achieved profitability by the sixth month, and maintained a ROAS above 10. They were selling only two core products initially: a basic essential bottom and plain bedding.
b076459471.e: ConPulse | How To Build A Sustainable D2C Brand with Mahesh Tekwani, Founder at Saadaa.

8dabe6cf29.q: Why did cotton yarn price increase impact Saadaa's home furnishing business and how did the company respond
8dabe6cf29.a: In 2021, during the COVID second wave, cotton yarn prices shot up by 2.5x, putting significant pressure on the home furnishing business. Rather than increase prices to consumers which would violate their values, Saadaa decided not to pass on the cost increase. This revealed that the buying pattern and consumption in home furnishing was very different from apparel, with consumers unwilling to pay significantly more, prompting them to focus the business model on apparel instead.
8dabe6cf29.e: ConPulse | How To Build A Sustainable D2C Brand with Mahesh Tekwani, Founder at Saadaa.

614e1ddee1.q: What is Mahesh Tekwani's framework for hiring and building a team at a D2C brand
614e1ddee1.a: Mahesh focuses on hiring people with two primary traits: a strong learning habit and self-organization. Rather than prioritizing performance and skill set alone, he emphasizes attitude, value system, and behavior—particularly a doer mentality and sense of ownership. He uses a two-axis framework evaluating both performance/skill and attitude/behavior, intentionally weighting attitude and self-learning culture more heavily than traditional corporate performance metrics.
614e1ddee1.e: ConPulse | How To Build A Sustainable D2C Brand with Mahesh Tekwani, Founder at Saadaa.

32e5635990.q: How does Saadaa differentiate its D2C strategy through packaging and brand storytelling
32e5635990.a: Saadaa does not use plastic packaging; instead, all products are sold in reusable cotton bags made from waste fabric, with stitching done by partner NGOs rather than at mass scale. Product tags are plantable seed paper that customers can grow into plants. These decisions directly impact margins—cotton bags cost over 40 rupees compared to 3 rupees for plastic—but reflect core brand values. The company translates this philosophy to employees through town halls sharing stories and actions, ensuring the vision aligns across products, team, and customer experience.
32e5635990.e: ConPulse | How To Build A Sustainable D2C Brand with Mahesh Tekwani, Founder at Saadaa.

aeb5d67838.q: What is the critical insight about economies of scale for D2C brands scaling from micro to large
aeb5d67838.a: Economies of scale operate as a bell curve, not a linear function. When very small, costs are low and margins are strong like a Kirana store. During the transitional growth phase, costs increase significantly due to administration and team building. Eventually at very large scale, costs plateau and margins improve. From micro to large scale, D2C founders face sustained margin pressure and cost increments and must maintain patience with the team, as compounding results appear only after extended effort.
aeb5d67838.e: ConPulse | How To Build A Sustainable D2C Brand with Mahesh Tekwani, Founder at Saadaa.

195837b6da.q: Why did Saadaa focus exclusively on a single product for extended periods and what was the payoff
195837b6da.a: Saadaa sold cotton pants as a single product for a year from August 2020 to December 2022, during which time the company did not grow even 1%. All effort was focused on building the right team, infrastructure, and culture. However, once these foundations were in place, growth recently kicked in—the team tripled from 30 people in March to 100 people, and revenue more than tripled in four months, demonstrating the compounding impact of patience and infrastructure investment.
195837b6da.e: ConPulse | How To Build A Sustainable D2C Brand with Mahesh Tekwani, Founder at Saadaa.

2f4a62f87c.q: What are the top growth opportunities and consumer behaviors when launching a brand in the Middle East market?
2f4a62f87c.a: The Middle East market has huge opportunity with high purchasing power consumers. Unlike US, China, or India, the market is smaller but consumers earn more and don't mind spending additional money to buy online. Key differences include time-saving preference: instead of spending 4-5 hours in malls, consumers can get delivery within 1-2 hours in UAE, Qatar, and Bahrain. People are willing to pay delivery charges even for short distances. The opportunity is still largely untapped with many brands focusing offline rather than online.
2f4a62f87c.e: ConPulse | How to Launch Your Brand In the Middle East Market with Shan Abdul Salam, Founder & CEO at Swish.

e06a16512e.q: How should new brands entering the Middle East market build distribution partnerships without local presence?
e06a16512e.a: Use the friends and family route to find connections in offline stores and hypermarkets. Get introduced to major clients of distributors, then connect with the distributor directly. BNI (Business Network International) is a very popular network group in the Middle East similar to Rotary in India—tapping into BNI networks can unlock partnership opportunities. The key is that everything runs on contacts and relationships; finding the right distributor who already has warehouse setup, manpower, and supermarket chain connections saves time and money.
e06a16512e.e: ConPulse | How to Launch Your Brand In the Middle East Market with Shan Abdul Salam, Founder & CEO at Swish.

ebb420cfc4.q: What is the WhatsApp strategy for customer engagement and review collection in Middle East ecommerce?
ebb420cfc4.a: After customer purchase, send review requests via WhatsApp. This strategy has shown 15% personal conversion rate compared to email's 1% conversion rate—for every 100 review requests sent via WhatsApp, at least 15 replies are received. People browse WhatsApp more than Google and receive constant notifications. Replies are almost always positive 5-star reviews with detailed feedback on delivery, customer service quality, and product satisfaction, allowing brands to understand what's working and double down on strengths.
ebb420cfc4.e: ConPulse | How to Launch Your Brand In the Middle East Market with Shan Abdul Salam, Founder & CEO at Swish.

1694d5d62c.q: What are the recommended categories and initial focus areas for new brand launches in the Middle East?
1694d5d62c.a: Pet care is identified as a huge market with extremely high consumer spending. Pet owners are ready to spend anything on their pets. While the market is small in population, the buying power and spending capacity of pet owners is enormous. Beyond category selection, focus on influencer marketing with influencers who match your brand's vision and have regional influence, and build partnerships with distributors for offline visibility in major hypermarkets and supermarkets.
1694d5d62c.e: ConPulse | How to Launch Your Brand In the Middle East Market with Shan Abdul Salam, Founder & CEO at Swish.

94f023ee43.q: How should Indian D2C brands scale into the Middle East without establishing a full local team?
94f023ee43.a: Find one resource who knows the market and has done it before—that resource solves everything else. Identify a distributor for offline stocking and online presence support. The brand already knows digital marketing and D2C operations from India, so leverage existing capabilities: a small warehouse team can pack and send via logistics partners for 1-2 hour delivery, while after-sales support and customer service can be handled from India using existing call center teams. This approach minimizes cash burn in the initial phase.
94f023ee43.e: ConPulse | How to Launch Your Brand In the Middle East Market with Shan Abdul Salam, Founder & CEO at Swish.

90a625357c.q: What government policy and payment gateway challenges exist for ecommerce businesses in Middle East regions?
90a625357c.a: Government policies and regulations in the Middle East are generally favorable and not a major delay factor. However, payment gateway experiences vary significantly: Dubai has very good payment gateway user experience, while Saudi Arabia and Qatar have payment gateway challenges and triple verification steps. Overall, the government is receptive and regulations are easy to work with once entrepreneurs find the right resource to navigate them.
90a625357c.e: ConPulse | How to Launch Your Brand In the Middle East Market with Shan Abdul Salam, Founder & CEO at Swish.

75acc50794.q: What are the three critical factors for e-commerce brand growth from zero to one stage?
75acc50794.a: The journey of zero to one involves three critical things that must move together: capital, inventory, and fulfillment. At the center of these three elements, you have quality given to your consumer. When these three things are properly coordinated like three balls rolling together, your brand automatically has an upward shift. Additionally, getting the product correct through need gap analysis is the most important lever, followed by availability and price positioning.
75acc50794.e: ConPulse | Investment Fundamentals - For E-commerce Founders with Nikunj Kansara, CEO & Co-Founder at First Ventures

d9163ec516.q: How has the e-commerce ecosystem in India evolved post-COVID in terms of success rates and competition?
d9163ec516.a: Before COVID, e-commerce was minimal and anything listed on platforms would sell, with standard 30% monthly growth. Post-COVID, the landscape completely evolved as everyone recognized the importance of selling online. Today, out of a hundred brands, only two or three are successful while 95% fail. This increased competition means brands now need fundamental operational practices in place to succeed, unlike the pre-2018 period when simply listing a product would lead to pickup regardless of category.
d9163ec516.e: ConPulse | Investment Fundamentals - For E-commerce Founders with Nikunj Kansara, CEO & Co-Founder at First Ventures

a6c53b6ef0.q: What is the strategic difference between D2C websites and marketplace sales channels for e-commerce brands?
a6c53b6ef0.a: D2C websites require heavy investment in marketing, audience acquisition, and traffic generation through social media and performance marketing; when marketing stops, ROAS starts fluctuating. Marketplaces like Amazon and Flipkart have ready audiences already present on the platform. However, both channels eradicate the traditional stockist-to-retail layer. The key difference is that D2C provides consumer data and direct customer insights, while marketplaces give access to existing traffic but limited consumer data—both complement each other and neither can survive alone long-term.
a6c53b6ef0.e: ConPulse | Investment Fundamentals - For E-commerce Founders with Nikunj Kansara, CEO & Co-Founder at First Ventures

a66a48751d.q: What are the main new-age challenges for e-commerce brands today regarding conversion and discovery?
a66a48751d.a: The primary challenge is conversion: with so many options available to consumers, conversion remains difficult for brands. To overcome this, brands must spend more on advertising and be available across multiple channels and locations to increase visibility. The second critical challenge is compliance and taxation, particularly GST filing, which becomes increasingly problematic as the brand grows. A third issue is understanding dispatch timelines and consumer delivery expectations, as there is confusion about when products actually reach consumers.
a66a48751d.e: ConPulse | Investment Fundamentals - For E-commerce Founders with Nikunj Kansara, CEO & Co-Founder at First Ventures

be2fd9de90.q: How should e-commerce founders approach unit economics and profitability at scale?
be2fd9de90.a: Founders must shift from order-level profitability to balance sheet-level profitability; you cannot expect every single order to be profitable. Get sourcing costs correct because products do not fail—costing does. Build a sustainable route with a strong operations team in place before marketing heavily, so the operations team can handle the pressure when you market. Finally, keep tight reconciliation checks: verify that the product was actually sent and received by the consumer and track exactly how much you paid for logistics, as this is critical to achieving unit economics positive.
be2fd9de90.e: ConPulse | Investment Fundamentals - For E-commerce Founders with Nikunj Kansara, CEO & Co-Founder at First Ventures

87d7cbeade.q: How many brands has First Ventures worked with over its operational history?
87d7cbeade.a: Over the past seven years, First Ventures has touched base with more than 800 brands, manufacturers, and importers end-to-end. The company also pioneered training as a concept in e-commerce specifically for Amazon and positions itself as a knowledge point for end-to-end solutions for all e-commerce needs both locally and globally.

a8296e8f41.q: What percentage of U.S. e-commerce revenue typically concentrates in the 10 days between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday?
a8296e8f41.a: For one company where Jennifer Alexander worked, the period just before Thanksgiving to just after Cyber Monday represented 30% of quarterly revenue in just about 10 days out of the 90 days in Q4. This highlights how critical seasonality is for direct-to-consumer brands in the U.S. market.

56c9c1ac6a.q: What is the current size and growth rate of the U.S. retail e-commerce market?
56c9c1ac6a.a: Retail e-commerce in the U.S. is about $900 billion and is growing at approximately 7% per year, making up 15% of total retail. This compares to overall retail growth of only 1% to 2%. The U.S. represents about 14% of total worldwide e-commerce, making it the second-largest market after China.
56c9c1ac6a.e: ConPulse | Secrets to grow your E-commerce brand in the USA with Jennifer Alexander

09cf1b07c1.q: What percentage of Americans shop online and what is the penetration of internet access in U.S. households?
09cf1b07c1.a: 90% of U.S. households have internet access, which is among the highest in the world. However, only 70% of Americans actually shop online, indicating there is still untapped market potential among those with internet access who do not yet transact online.

b3f977925f.q: How much of e-commerce transactions in the United States now occur on mobile devices?
b3f977925f.a: Mobile commerce accounts for approximately 30% to 40% of online purchases, and this number has grown significantly over the last five to six years. This mobile penetration continues to grow as consumers increasingly make purchases on their phones while on the go.
b3f977925f.e: ConPulse | Secrets to grow your E-commerce brand in the USA with Jennifer Alexander

d43d0ac979.q: What percentage of U.S. consumers purchase Christmas presents online?
d43d0ac979.a: 60% of the U.S. population buys Christmas presents online, making the holiday season a distinctly important and concentrated revenue period for e-commerce brands, particularly in the United States compared to other markets worldwide.
d43d0ac979.e: ConPulse | Secrets to grow your E-commerce brand in the USA with Jennifer Alexander

f8d71b9dbc.q: What key consumer expectation distinguishes the U.S. e-commerce market from other markets?
f8d71b9dbc.a: Authenticity is the most critical element when launching a brand in the U.S., where countless new brands enter daily across Amazon, Etsy, and direct-to-consumer channels. Consumers want to know who is behind the brand, whether products are made locally or overseas, and the authentic story behind how the product came to market, making your About Us page critically important.
f8d71b9dbc.e: ConPulse | Secrets to grow your E-commerce brand in the USA with Jennifer Alexander

2f930812fc.q: How should e-commerce brands understand product pricing and consumer buying behavior across different product categories?
2f930812fc.a: High-end lipstick might retail for $18 while low-end costs $2-3, creating very different unit economics and shipping strategies. An impulse buy like a low-cost lipstick requires different handling than an expensive moisturizer or electronic device, which typically require multiple visits, research, and visits to competing sites before purchase. Understanding this consumer journey and buying lifecycle is fundamentally critical to building authentic brand experiences.
2f930812fc.e: ConPulse | Secrets to grow your E-commerce brand in the USA with Jennifer Alexander

1e212ced06.q: What marketing spend allocation framework should e-commerce brands use to balance stability and innovation?
1e212ced06.a: Jennifer Alexander uses the 70-20-10 framework originally from Google: spend 70% of advertising budget on core work projects that drive the majority of your business, 20% on related initiatives, and 10% on testing new channels. For most e-commerce brands, the 70% typically goes to paid search, retargeting ads, and email, while the remaining 30% tests product carousels, social ads, AI, payment options, and emerging technologies.
1e212ced06.e: ConPulse | Secrets to grow your E-commerce brand in the USA with Jennifer Alexander

bb1d8f2b50.q: How do subscription and save programs perform in the U.S. e-commerce market?
bb1d8f2b50.a: Subscribe and save programs, like Amazon's famous offering, still only make up about 5% to 15% of total business depending on the category, and even for consumable products like dog food that people buy regularly, adoption remains low. U.S. consumers often prefer the choice and convenience of ordering when they want rather than committing to automatic recurring shipments.
bb1d8f2b50.e: ConPulse | Secrets to grow your E-commerce brand in the USA with Jennifer Alexander

8126ab10a3.q: What is the dominant payment method for U.S. online shoppers and what emerging payment options are gaining traction?
8126ab10a3.a: Credit cards still dominate as the primary payment method for U.S. e-commerce consumers. However, digital wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay are increasingly popular, and split payment options like Affirm, which breaks payments into four installments, are also gaining adoption as alternative payment methods.
